articles.title: Snap tries to make the case again for its $2,200 smart glasses | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Since Specs' debut earlier this year, Snap has clearly been looking for an opportunity to explain why the smart glasses deserve to exist.
articles.body:
When Snap debuted its long-awaited smart glasses, Specs, earlier this year, the reveal was not only underwhelming but also a genuine disaster. The glasses — which cost a whopping $2,200 and are vaguely reminiscent of scuba gear — inspired jeers online and calls for the company’s CEO, Evan Spiegel, to resign. The company’s stock subsequently nosedived .

Since then, Snap has clearly been looking for an opportunity to explain why Specs — a heavy, expensive piece of hardware that most casual consumers will probably be unable to afford — deserves to exist.

This week, the company had its chance to make that argument. At an event in Los Angeles, Spiegel and other Snap executives unveiled a variety of new features and services connected to Specs. The new updates seem clearly designed to help integrate the glasses into a broader array of digital activities and, in doing so, give Specs a clearer sense of purpose.

During Wednesday’s event, Spiegel shared details about a number of the new features. After a trippy promotional video that vaguely brought to mind an ayahuasca hallucination, the CEO took the stage and began a series of live demos.

New entertainment options — Specs can now connect with HBO Max and Spotify — provide a baseline of interactive fun that smart glasses have largely lacked until now.

Yet perhaps the biggest announcement was the launch of Specs Intelligence, which the company calls a new “anticipatory AI” system designed to pair not only with the company’s glasses but also with user devices — including iPhones and Macs. Snap claims that this new system “builds an understanding of your goals, priorities, relationships, and routines from the apps and tools you choose to connect, helping you focus on what matters now while making progress towards your longer-term goals.”

Spiegel called this system an “AI native operating system with intelligence designed around your projects” that helps users “connect the dots across Lenses,” Snap’s term for its AR camera effects, available on both phones and Specs, “so you can get things done while focusing on what matters to you.” In practice, it seems to function more like an AI productivity app that can be used with Snap’s glasses but doesn’t require them.

Snap has also announced a new program called Specs for Enterprise, which allows the device to be integrated into corporate workflows. On Wednesday, the company announced partnerships with a number of different tech companies — including Amazon, Salesforce, Nvidia, and other firms — in an effort to make the device useful to staff at those companies.

What is the real-world utility of this, and who is this service really for? Apparently, the answer is IT technicians. While the actual scenarios in which Specs can be used are a little vague, a demo video played at the event showed an IT technician repairing some hardware with the help of Snap’s new glasses.

“We’re building out mobile device management, security controls, and ways to deploy and manage stacks across teams with the world’s most trusted providers, bringing peace of mind to IT departments,” Spiegel said.

Other announced features were slightly more head-scratching. For instance, one of the new experiences is an app, developed through a partnership with the NBA and WNBA, that allows users to practice basketball and improve their shot via the glasses’ AR capabilities. But, realistically, who is really going to play basketball while wearing heavy goggles on their head?

Also announced Wednesday was a new connectivity package for anyone who wants to use Specs on the go, away from Wi-Fi — like outside the home or office. Sold separately, the package includes a charging case with built-in cellular connectivity. That connectivity, which is being made available via a partnership with Verizon, costs $10 a month for Verizon customers and $20 a month for non-Verizon customers.

Spiegel ultimately framed Specs as a new way to engage with computing in a more human-centric format. “I will say it’s an interesting time to be launching a new computer because things in tech are pretty weird right now,” Spiegel said. “We’re being told that AI will take our jobs, that virtual worlds will replace the real one. Well, no, thank you. We do not accept that future. Making people irrelevant is not progress, and computers should make us more important, not less.”

Snap has repeatedly justified the product’s cringe-inducing cost by characterizing the device as a computer — albeit one you wear on your face. Whether consumers will go for that or not remains to be seen. The company has announced that it is hosting a Specs pop-up in Los Angeles in October before the devices ultimately ship later this fall.

articles.title: ‘South Park’ Season 29 Premiere Embraces ‘South America’ Name Change With New Theme Song and a Trump Cameo
articles.summary: “South Park” — or rather “South America” — made its Season 29 debut Wednesday night and wasted no time introducing audiences to the newly named town. The epi...
articles.body:
"South Park" — or rather "South America" — made its Season 29 debut Wednesday night and wasted no time introducing audiences to the newly named town.

The episode, titled "South American Biker Gangs," kicked off with an updated theme song ringing in the name change — "I'm goin' down to South America, have myself a time!" — before showing another new addition: a Donald Trump cameo.

The premiere episode centered around the usual suspects, Cartman, Stan, Kyle and Kenny, and their newfound love of e-bikes. But when the gaggle of kids takes to the streets with their motorized bikes, the parents of South America form their own biker gang in opposition.

As per usual, Kenny dies when his e-bike blows up, and his death unites the town to come together, outlaw e-bikes and begin selling "South America Strong" T-shirts.

Earlier this month, ahead of the Season 29 premiere, creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone announced that the long-running comedy series would furthermore be known as "South America," a comedic jab at Trump's recent moves to rename the likes of Lake Ontario as Lake America, New Mexico as New America and the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America.

"Inspired by the bravery and patriotism of Apple and Google, we are changing the name of 'South Park' to 'South America,'" the pair shared in a statement. "We especially want to thank our parent company Paramount — a Skydance Capitulation."

The show took home the gold for outstanding animated program at the 2026 Creative Arts Emmys, and while celebrating the win, threw another dig at Trump by sharing a graphic of the president with his pants and underwear around his ankles to the official "South Park" X account.

The moves are a continuation of the show's Season 28 political antics, which included plot points like JD Vance seducing Donald Trump in order to dodge punishment for trying to kill his unborn baby with Satan and Pete Hegseth trying to bust Peter Thiel out of jail.

articles.title: Who left 'Dancing With the Stars' last night? 2nd celebrity sent home.
articles.summary: The competition has already lost two celebrities after a two-night Season 35 premiere.
articles.body:
Dancing With the Stars is back for Season 35 — but two celebrities' bids for the mirror ball trophy have already come to an end.

The ABC show kicked off Tuesday night with a new group of celebrities hoping to follow in the footsteps of Season 34 champion Robert Irwin.

This year's cast includes reality TV stars, actors, athletes, musicians and familiar faces from across the entertainment industry, including Summer House star Ciara Miller, 10 Things I Hate About You actor Julia Stiles, The Traitors ' Maura Higgins and singer Taylor Hanson.

Carrie Ann Inaba, Derek Hough and Bruno Tonioli are back at the judges' table, with Alfonso Ribeiro and Julianne Hough returning as hosts for their fourth consecutive season.

But after two nights of performances — and two eliminations — the competition has already narrowed. So, who was the latest celebrity sent home? Here's what happened.

Who was eliminated from 'Dancing With the Stars' last night?

Influencer Sarah Jane Nader and her professional partner, Hailey Bills, became the second pair eliminated from Season 35 on Wednesday.

The pair performed a jive to Avril Lavigne's "Sk8er Boi," earning a total score of 14 out of 30 from judges Carrie Ann Inaba, Derek Hough and Bruno Tonioli.

Their score was combined with viewer votes, but it wasn't enough to secure them a place in week two.

Nader and Bills were the third same-sex pairing to appear in the show's 35-season run. "I think that us being on this ballroom floor together as two women is just so powerful," Nader said after her routine. "And I hope that it shows you can dance with whoever you want, you can love whoever you want, and being yourself is the best power."

The influencer's sister, Brooks, competed on DWTS in 2024 and finished in ninth place.

Who was the 1st celebrity eliminated from 'Dancing With the Stars'?

Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star Conner Leavitt and Adele Zaikman were the first pair eliminated from Season 35 during Tuesday's opening night.

They performed a salsa to Tag Team's "Whoomp! (There It Is)," receiving 4s from all three judges for a total score of 12 out of 30.

"This has been the most fun," Leavitt said after being voted off. "I have the greatest dance partner in the world in Adele. I can't wait for the world to get to see her talent."

Zaikman added, "It's a dream come true no matter what, and I'm so lucky that I had Conner. I had so much fun, and thank you so much for everything."

What happened with 'Dancing With the Stars' voting?

Tuesday night's premiere was hit by technical problems when the show's online voting system crashed during the live broadcast.

Julianne Hough initially told viewers that online voting was temporarily unavailable and encouraged them to vote by text. Alfonso Ribeiro later announced that online votes would be thrown out for the night, meaning only votes submitted by text would count.

Online voting was restored for Wednesday's episode.

Who topped the 'Dancing With the Stars' leaderboard?

Harry Shum Jr. and Jenna Johnson, and Maura Higgins and Mark Ballas, finished premiere week tied at the top of the leaderboard with 21 points each.

Shum and Johnson earned their score Tuesday for a cha cha to Earth, Wind & Fire's "Let's Groove."

Higgins and Ballas matched them Wednesday with a foxtrot to Alannah Myles's "Black Velvet."

When is 'Dancing With the Stars' on again?

Following the two-night premiere, Dancing With the Stars returns to its regular schedule Tuesday, Sept. 22, at 8 p.m. ET on ABC and Disney+.

Episodes are available to stream the following day on Hulu.

articles.title: Bose’s next open earbuds have more bass, more volume, and more battery life
articles.summary: Bose helped start the clip-on earbud trend, and its second-gen Ultra Open Earbuds deliver improved sound and battery life with a redesigned charging case.
articles.body: Bose announced a new version of its Ultra Open Earbuds that helped kick off the industry trend of clip-on wireless earbuds nearly two-and-a-half years ago. The new Ultra Open Earbuds (2nd Gen) feature a subtle redesign with improved performance in both sound quality and battery life. They’re also joined by a new cheaper alternative called the Bose Sport Open Earbuds designed to provide a more secure and stable fit during physical activities. The Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (2nd Gen) will be available for preorder on September 19th for $299 with availability starting on October 1st. Color options include black, white smoke, cherry chocolate, olive green, and sky pink. Preorders and availability for the Bose Sport Open Earbuds are the same, but they’re $100 cheaper at $199. Colors include black, white smoke, and eucalyptus green. [Image: The design of the Ultra Open Earbuds (2nd Gen) remains mostly the same aside from aesthetic improvements. Like the original version, the new Ultra Open Earbuds (2nd Gen) feature a design that clips to your outer ear with a transducer that directs audio into your ear canal with “minimal sound leakage,” Bose claims. There’s still no ANC because these are designed to do the exact opposite and let you hear what’s going on around you while enjoying music or a podcast. In addition to a refreshed design with a new beveled finish on each earbud’s metal cap, the 2nd Gen feature a new driver delivering higher volume with automatic adjustments and deeper bass. A new Cinema Mode simulates a “wider, more immersive soundstage” using Bose’s TrueSpatial technology while keeping dialogue clear and centered. Battery life with the buds alone has been boosted to up to nine hours (from seven hours) with an additional 19.5 hours of playback from the redesigned case that can now stand upright for use on a wireless charger. [Image: An added bumpy texture on the Sport Open Earbuds’ customizable buttons makes them easier to locate by touch. The Bose Sport Open Earbuds take a similar approach with a design that clips to your ear to project sounds inward, but they feature a thinner cuff with a “soft silicone matte finish” providing more grip to keep them in place. Bose says the Sport version will stay secure during head shakes, cartwheels, and running. They also feature automatic volume adjustments that adapt to ambient noise levels to ensure what you’re listening to isn’t drowned out, and the customizable shortcut button on the end of each battery barrel has an added texture, so they’re easier to find while working out. Battery life is rated at up to seven hours of playback plus an additional 22 hours with the wireless charging case.

articles.title: Apple's iPhones go Pro, their prices go Pro Max; but why most buyers may still pay
articles.summary: Tech News News: For years, Apple made the iPhone more accessible in India without making it cheap. Older models stayed on sale, bank offers softened the sticker price.
articles.body: For years, Apple made the iPhone more accessible in India without making it cheap. Older models stayed on sale, bank offers softened the sticker price, exchange programmes rewarded upgrades and no-cost EMIs converted a large purchase into manageable monthly payments. That carefully constructed ladder is now becoming steeper.Apple’s latest pricing pushes the iPhone further beyond the reach of many Indian buyers. The iPhone 18 Pro starts at Rs 1,64,900, while the Pro Max begins at Rs 1,79,900. The new foldable iPhone Duo occupies another universe altogether: Rs 2,99,900 for the base variant, rising to Rs 4,49,900 with 2TB storage.But the affordability problem is not confined to Apple’s most experimental phone. The iPhone 17 now starts at Rs 99,900, the 17e at Rs 79,900 and the iPhone Air at Rs 1,49,900. Even buying last year’s phone no longer guarantees a substantially cheaper entry into Apple’s ecosystem.India has reportedly received some of Apple’s steepest price increases this year. Prices of certain models have risen by as much as 41%, as the company responds to higher memory and storage costs. The increases are especially striking because India is simultaneously becoming an important iPhone manufacturing and export base.Affordability wall gets tallerThe case that the iPhone is becoming unaffordable is straightforward. India remains a price-sensitive smartphone market where most devices are sold well below Rs 30,000. An iPhone costing Rs 1 lakh or more therefore competes not merely with other phones but with laptops, motorcycles, household appliances, holidays and, in the Duo’s case, even entry-level cars.The Pro models pose the more important test. The Duo will always be a niche showcase designed for wealthy early adopters. But the Pro and Pro Max have become central to Apple’s image and annual upgrade cycle. Once their prices move towards Rs 2 lakh after adding storage, protection plans and accessories, even affluent professionals may question whether the improvements justify the outlay.This is particularly relevant when phones are lasting longer. Premium processors remain capable for years, software support has improved and annual camera or display upgrades are often incremental. A customer using an iPhone 15 Pro or 16 Pro may see little urgency in spending another Rs 1.6–2 lakh.Higher prices could therefore change behaviour without immediately destroying demand. Consumers may retain phones longer, buy refurbished devices, seek overseas purchases or wait for online sales. Some may move from Pro models to the standard iPhone, while first-time buyers could choose older inventory through third-party retailers rather than Apple’s current lineup.There is also a risk that financing conceals rather than solves the affordability problem. An EMI can make a Rs 1.8-lakh phone appear manageable, but it does not reduce its cost. Stretching repayment periods for a rapidly depreciating device can turn aspiration into financial strain.Why most buyers may still payYet Apple has repeatedly shown that conventional affordability calculations do not fully explain premium-phone demand in India. An iPhone is not bought solely for its processor, camera or display. It carries social and aspirational value, signals professional success and provides entry into an ecosystem of watches, earbuds, computers and services. For many upwardly mobile buyers, owning an iPhone remains a visible marker of having arrived.That appeal has helped Apple grow even when considerably cheaper Android phones offer comparable specifications. The iPhone 16 became India’s bestselling smartphone during the final quarter of 2025, demonstrating that Apple can generate mass demand when it combines an aspirational product with festive discounts, bank offers and exchange incentives.India’s premium smartphone market has also expanded even as the broader market has struggled. Consumers who previously bought phones costing Rs 30,000–40,000 have moved upwards, helped by financing and rising expectations around cameras, gaming, durability and brand value. For these buyers, a phone is used frequently enough to justify spending more than on many other personal possessions.Apple benefits from unusually strong resale values as well. An iPhone may cost more upfront, but it generally retains more value than many competing devices. Exchange bonuses reduce the effective upgrade price for existing users, while long software support allows buyers to spread the cost over four or five years.The Duo could reinforce rather than weaken this aspirational pull. Its price makes it inaccessible to most consumers, but exclusivity is part of its proposition. Like an expensive watch or luxury handbag, it may attract buyers precisely because it is uncommon and instantly recognisable. Apple does not need it to become a mass-market product for it to strengthen the brand.The more likely outcome, therefore, is not that Indians stop buying iPhones. It is that the market becomes more sharply divided. Wealthier customers and committed Apple users will continue buying Pro and Duo models, often assisted by trade-ins and instalments. More aspirational buyers will wait for discounts, purchase older generations or enter through refurbished devices.The iPhone is moving out of reach at its official prices. But that does not necessarily put it out of desire. In India’s premium market, the distance between what consumers can comfortably afford and what they are willing to pay has always been where Apple does its best business.Get the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: Huawei plans Q1 2027 launch of new AI chip as it takes on Nvidia | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Huawei is accelerating the launch of its next-generation Ascend 960DT AI chip as it pushes to compete with Nvidia and close China’s AI computing gap with the U.S.
articles.body:
Huawei is moving up the launch of its next-generation Ascend 960DT AI chip to the first quarter of 2027, as it races to challenge Nvidia, the company said on Thursday at its Huawei Connect conference.

The Chinese tech giant had previously planned to launch the chip in Q3 of 2027, a Huawei spokesperson told TechCrunch.

“The Ascend 960DT is expected to be ready in Q1 2027. Ascend 960 chips are launching ahead of schedule, doubling performance and advancing year by year,” the spokesperson said, adding that David Wang, Huawei’s rotating and acting chairman, announced the updated timeline at Huawei Connect on Thursday.

The announcement comes just a week before U.S. President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping are set to meet on September 24 in Washington, DC.

Huawei is trying to turn hundreds of thousands, and eventually millions, of AI chips into one giant computer. The Chinese tech firm calls the approach its Peerium Computing Architecture. It relies on UnifiedBus, Huawei’s technology for linking processors with memory, storage, and networking hardware. Eric Xu, Huawei’s rotating chairman, said in the company’s statement that it is using its new Peerium Computing Architecture to build larger AI computing systems designed for both training and inference.

Huawei’s Atlas 950 SuperPoD and SuperCluster are the first systems based on the architecture. The company says an Atlas 950 SuperCluster can connect up to 256,000 accelerator cards.

The accelerated chip timeline comes with some questions about Huawei’s broader AI systems, however. China tech analyst Rui Ma said on X that Huawei had previously said its Atlas 960 SuperPoD would scale to 15,488 Ascend 960 chips, while this week’s announcement referred to a system with 4,096 chips. “The chip itself is coming WAY earlier, but the SuperPoD they announced is much smaller than what they originally laid out,” Ma wrote.

Huawei has continued to advance its chip ambitions despite U.S. restrictions on China’s access to advanced semiconductor technology. Ma said that those restrictions are unlikely to stop China from pursuing its own semiconductor technology.

“I think it’s futile to stop China’s development in semiconductors because the stakes for self-sufficiency are just too high at this point,” she wrote.

Trump has pushed back against calls from AI industry leaders to slow the development of the technology over safety concerns, arguing that the U.S. needs to maintain its lead over China. Meanwhile, Xu argued that China needs to accelerate AI development to catch up with the U.S., saying Chinese companies need to advance further before they can fully understand and address the risks posed by more powerful AI systems, according to Financial Times.

articles.title: Camp Snap’s 110D gives slim retro film cameras a digital upgrade
articles.summary: The Camp Snap 110D’s slim, horizontal design looks straight out of the ‘70s but features an 8-megapixel sensor and microSD storage.
articles.body: Camp Snap is expanding its small collection of screenless digital point-and-shoot cameras with the new pocket-friendly 110D featuring a thin horizontal design first popularized by Kodak film cameras in the 1970s. The Camp Snap 110D is available for preorder starting today for $74.95 in back in black (black and gray) or dreamsicle (white and orange) color options with matching accessories. The Camp Snap 110D’s design is inspired by the myriad of low-cost cameras from companies like Canon, Minolta, and Pentax that used the 110 film cartridges Kodak first introduced in 1972. The cartridges were easy for even novice photographers to use and could be developed using existing machines already capable of processing 16mm motion picture film. Lomography is one of the last companies to still manufacture 110 film, but the Camp Snap 110D offers a similar experience with the convenience of digital. [Image: At launch, the 110D is available in two color options, although with other models, Camp Snap later expanded the number of color options available. Like the Camp Snap 2 that launched last June, the 110D isn’t a megapixel powerhouse. It uses an 8-megapixel Sony 1/3.2-inch CMOS sensor paired with a 4.2mm, f/2.0 lens that’s compatible with 30.5mm screw-on filters if you want to experiment with wide-angle or macro photography. If you’re after a matching retro look for your photos, the 110D includes five built-in software filters with vintage, analog, and black and white effects that are selectable using a sliding switch. [Image: The 110D relies on an optical viewfinder, and there’s no way to see your shots until you’ve copied them to a computer or your phone. The 4GB bundled microSD card, which is stored behind a screw-secured door so kids can’t find it, can store up to 2,000 photos before you need to copy them off to a mobile device or PC over USB-C. The 110D’s 800mAh battery has enough capacity for around 500 shots while an automatic sleep mode that quickly wakes the camera when the shutter button is pressed helps prevent unwanted battery drain without having to constantly power the 110D off an on. Other features include a built-in flash with adjustable color temperature and a basic segmented LCD display on the back showing remaining battery life and the number of photos you’ve taken.

articles.title: I tried Tovala's smart oven for two weeks — here's whether it beats takeout | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Tovala offers both a smart oven and a meal-delivery service. Its meals come with QR codes that you scan using the app, allowing the oven to automatically follow the cooking instructions.
articles.body:
I tried Tovala’s smart oven for two weeks to see if it could actually make dinner as easy as the company promises. It won’t replace the quality of a good home-cooked meal, and some dishes turned out better than others, but it’s hard to beat the convenience on days when you absolutely don’t want to cook.

This was exactly the challenge that Tovala co-founder and CEO David Rabie aimed to address.

“The idea originated from my own struggles in business school. I was often busy and sought a solution as convenient as takeout or frozen meals, yet still wanted the experience of a genuine home-cooked dish,” Rabie told TechCrunch via email.

“One afternoon, I was making a meal using several different appliances and realized that I was mostly just pressing buttons,” he said. “That’s what led to the idea for an end-to-end system: fresh, mostly prepped meals paired with a connected oven that could cook them automatically. The challenge became figuring out how to remove all that friction without sacrificing the experience of eating food that was actually cooked fresh at home.”

The idea is pretty simple: Tovala sends you meals with the ingredients already portioned out, and its smart oven handles the cooking.

Instead of chopping vegetables, measuring ingredients, figuring out cooking temperatures, and standing over a stove, you mostly just unwrap everything, follow simple instructions like adding packets of seasoning, put everything in the provided trays, scan a QR code using the companion app, and let the oven do the rest.

The countertop-sized oven follows the cooking instructions automatically, switching temperatures and cooking modes throughout the process. It can bake, broil, air fry, toast, and reheat. The regular oven costs $299, while the Smart Oven Pro costs $349 and adds a steam function.

As for the meal-delivery side, there are more than 45 meals to choose from each week. For instance, steak and garlic mashed potatoes, salmon with vegetables, butternut squash soup, pasta dishes, and more.

There are also plenty of options when it comes to how much food you want delivered. Meal plans include 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, or 16 meals per week. You can skip deliveries, pause your plan, or cancel if you don’t need meals that week.

The meals aren’t exactly cheap, though. Single-serving meals start at $13.99, and two-serving meals start at around $8.99 per serving — $17.98 total — plus a $10.99 shipping fee. The company also recently launched family-sized meals, starting at $35.96. Unlike meal-delivery rivals like HelloFresh, Tovala is essentially betting that you’re willing to pay for the added convenience of having most of the cooking handled for you.

Taste and quality were the parts I was most skeptical about going in. I’m not a professional chef by any means, but I’ve recently gotten much more interested in cooking. Once you start learning how to properly sear meat, roast vegetables, and build flavor yourself, it’s hard not to be suspicious of a machine that promises to do all of that for you.

The biggest downside for me was the texture of the meats and how they cooked in the oven. I like a steak with a nice crust, so I finished mine in a steel pan for some extra browning. The steak was much better afterward, but that obviously defeats the point of a process that’s supposed to be mostly hands-off.

Not every dish had that problem, though. One of my favorites was the pineapple shrimp stir-fry. The rice was well cooked, and the sauce had plenty of flavor. It wasn’t necessarily something I’d rave about compared with a great restaurant meal, but it was easy, satisfying, and required very little effort.

What I appreciated most, however, was the grocery-food feature that gives the oven some use beyond cooking Tovala-branded meals. The oven can recognize certain grocery-store products, so instead of guessing how long your frozen waffles need to toast, you can scan the barcode and let the oven automatically select the appropriate settings.

That’s what makes Tovala feel more like a genuinely smart oven, not just a machine built to cook its own meal kits. Even if you stop ordering Tovala meals, you can still use the oven with compatible grocery products.

Overall, if your alternative to cooking is ordering takeout because you’re too tired to cook, Tovala makes a pretty compelling case for itself.

Tovala is available on the company’s website and Amazon. It ships to most U.S. states, but it doesn’t currently ship to Alaska or Hawaii.

During the episode, Kapila spoke about facing domestic violence in her marriage. She made a shocking revelation about how her in-laws tried to set her on fire and separated her from her daughter. She added that the situation became so serious that she nearly lost her life.Kapil, who took to the hot seat in Wednesday's episode, spoke about her traumatic past. During the episode, host Amitabh Bachchan noticed scars on her face and neck and asked her about the reason behind them. Kapila further revealed that she survived an ‘agni-kaand’ in 2002, alleging that her in-laws tried to set her on fire.She also went on to share that her in-laws tortured her as her husband had married against the family’s will. She said she was separated from her daughter when the the latter was very young and she has not seen her in 24 years. She claimed that her in-laws stopped her from meeting her daughter. However, she later learnt from neighbours that her daughter had moved to another city for work. She said, “I pray for her every single day,” she said.Kapila recalled the incident and said that she was saved only because someone happened to arrive at the right time. She remained unconscious for more than two weeks after the incident. Once she regained consciousness, she filed a police complaint, and her surgeries began soon after.Kapila currently works as a home tutor and spends most of her time at home. When asked how she planned to use the prize money, she said she wants to undergo surgery for artificial ears. Waymo says it is “working toward offering fully autonomous ride-hailing to the public” by 2028. Waymo will need approval from Singapore’s Land Transport Authority (LTA) before it can begin accepting passengers. The city-state requires all autonomous vehicles to undergo a safety assessment conducted at the Centre of Excellence for Testing and Research (CETRAN) before they can be deployed on public roads. The tests have been developed by LTA and CETRAN, with input from the Traffic Police. But Waymo isn’t totally unknown in Singapore. The company established a corporate entity there earlier this year and participates in Singapore’s Steering Committee on Autonomous Vehicles. Singapore has become a hotbed for autonomous vehicle testing. The local authorities have green-lit autonomous freight delivery and road-sweepers, as well as self-driving buses for airport workers. Motional, a US-based company majority owned by Hyundai, conducted a robotaxi pilot in Singapore in 2016. In addition to Singapore, Waymo has said it plans on launching a robotaxi service in London by the end of 2026, and Tokyo in 2027. The company has also said it will bring its robotaxis to Munich, Germany, in late 2027, marking its first expansion in the European Union. “Singapore has built one of the safest, most efficient, and most forward-thinking transportation ecosystems in the world,” Waymo co-CEO Tekedra Mawakana said in a statement. “Their focus on reliability, sustainability, and human-centric progress directly mirrors how we have built Waymo’s technology and service.” This year, Waymo has announced several new domestic markets, including Nashville, Denver, San Diego, and Las Vegas. The company has around 4,000 vehicles operating in about 15 US cities. But regulatory hurdles and political opposition have kept it out of some of the US’ most important cities, including New York City, Chicago, and Washington, DC. As the robotaxi debate continues to rage on in America, Waymo has signaled that it intends to keep growing overseas — with no signs of slowing down.

articles.title: Watch: Long queues outside Apple stores across India as iPhone 18 series, 1st foldable iPhone go on sale
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Long queues formed outside Apple stores across India on Friday as customers turned up early to get their hands on the company’s latest prod.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Long queues formed outside Apple stores across India on Friday as customers turned up early to get their hands on the company’s latest products, including the iPhone 18 Pro series and its first-ever foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo.At a store in Bengaluru, customers began arriving as early as 5am, with buyers travelling from Haryana, Delhi and Mumbai for the launch. One customer, Rahul, said he had been buying iPhones for years and described the annual launch as a “festival”.In Noida, a buyer who had travelled from Punjab said he had been standing in the queue since 6am after booking two iPhone 18 Pro Max devices.The rush came despite the premium pricing of Apple’s latest lineup, which includes the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, AirPods 5, Apple Watch Series 12, Apple Watch Ultra 4 and the new foldable iPhone Duo.The iPhone 18 Pro starts at Rs 1,64,900 for the 256GB model, while the iPhone 18 Pro Max starts at Rs 1,79,900. Both models are available in 256GB, 512GB, 1TB and 2TB storage variants.The 18 Pro series comes in black, silver, glacier and a new burgundy finish. The phones feature a 48MP Fusion Main camera with variable aperture and new Pro camera controls. They are powered by Apple’s A20 Pro chip and a new vapour chamber aimed at improving performance, AI features and battery life.Apple says the iPhone 18 Pro Max offers the longest battery life of any Pro model.Apple's first foldable iPhoneThe iPhone Duo is the biggest new addition to Apple’s lineup and marks the company’s entry into the foldable smartphone segment.It features a 7.6-inch inner Super Retina XDR display and a 5.4-inch outer display. Apple says it is the thinnest iPhone when unfolded. The device is powered by the A20 Pro chip and comes with an advanced camera system, all-day battery life and new multitasking features.The Duo also supports dual-display experiences through iOS 27, along with Apple Intelligence and Siri.AirPods and Apple Watch updatesApple’s new AirPods 5 feature Active Noise Cancellation in an open-ear design. The company claims they remove up to 50% more outside noise than AirPods 4 with ANC.The earbuds also offer Adaptive EQ, hands-free Siri, Live Translation and Siri Interactions through head movements. The Wireless Charging Case version provides up to five hours of listening time with ANC.The Apple Watch Series 12 and Apple Watch Ultra 4 feature the S11 chip and Health Sensing System, along with heart-rate sensing, more frequent heart-rate and HRV readings and a new readiness score.The Series 12 offers up to 24 hours of battery life, while the Ultra 4 offers up to 50 hours and can track outdoor workouts for up to 45 hours.In India, pre-orders for the iPhone 18 Pro models began on September 12, while the AirPods 5 and new Apple Watches opened for pre-orders on September 9. articles.title: Raja D King’s ‘iPhone Langar’: 10 phones, 1,000 people and a ‘Jai Mata Di’ rule for Chandigarh event

articles.body: CHANDIGARH: After his earlier ‘petrol langar’ drew a large crowd in Chandigarh, social media personality Rakesh Trehan, also known as Raja D King, has announced that he will begin distributing iPhones on September 22, saying the recipients will be selected publicly.Trehan said the distribution will begin at the same location in Chandigarh and will be conducted live in front of the public and media.He said people from Chandigarh and Mohali will be among those selected initially, news agency PTI reported.“iPhones will be distributed live in front of everyone to selected people from Chandigarh and Mohali. The names of the lucky recipients will be drawn in front of everyone,” Trehan said.He said the initial group would comprise 1,000 people, all of whom would be considered for the distribution.“We had planned to distribute iPhone 16 and 17 models and go forward with newer models, but we dropped the idea as people who received iPhone 16 might complain to Mata Ji, questioning why he or she was not her favourite,” he said.Going forward with the idea, he then said that lucky winners will receive iPhone 17 models, depending on availability.Trehan also referred to his earlier event in Amritsar, where he claimed more than 3,000 people were part of the group and 484 gold coins were distributed, including 280 contributed by one individual, PTI reported.Trehan also laid down a condition for those seeking an iPhone, saying members of the group would have to write “Jai Mata Di” once every day until they receive the phone.He said those who forget to write it on a particular day could make up for it by writing it twice the following day.He said the activity would be monitored and those who failed to write the phrase would not be eligible to receive an iPhone.Trehan said he had initially planned to distribute 100 iPhones in Chandigarh and 200 in Mohali.However, he said 10 iPhones would be distributed on September 22 as part of the initial exercise, with the distribution to be expanded to 10 more cities in Punjab, PTI reported.He said people in the additional cities would be given around 12-13 days to prepare and fulfill the given requirements before the next date for distribution is announced on October 5.The announcement comes after Trehan’s earlier ‘petrol langar’ in Chandigarh was postponed due to heavy rain.The event had drawn a large crowd despite the postponement, with people expecting free fuel coupons. articles.title: I’m so mad that I love Orion's $2,195 AI mattress pad | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Sleeping on the Orion is like flipping your pillow to find “the cool side,” except that your entire bed is the cool side.
articles.body:
When Orion asked if I wanted to test its $2,195 AI-enabled mattress pad, I agreed purely because I thought it would be funny to write about. I mean, come on. What could possibly be “AI-enabled” about something you sleep on? And why does it cost more than my monthly rent in a major city?

The joke, as it turned out, was on me. Over the few months that I’ve had the Orion sleep system, I’ve been sleeping like a baby.

Orion is basically a cooling mattress pad that you can control using your phone, and it adjusts temperature as you sleep to minimize how often you wake up in the middle of the night. Sleeping on the pad feels like flipping your pillow to find “the cool side,” except that now your whole bed is the cool side of the pillow.

As for the AI aspect, Orion supposedly learns from your sleep data to modulate temperatures and maximize the quality of your sleep, though I’m skeptical of how necessary these AI features actually are (and how much they contribute to the hefty price tag).

By default, the Orion will start cooling down around the time you go to bed, which you manually input. It will then get colder as you fall asleep, and then when it’s time for you to wake up, it slowly brings the mattress pad back to room temperature, making it easier for you to get out of bed.

Orion’s founder Harry Gestetner is only 26 years old, but he’s more experienced as an entrepreneur than his age might suggest: He sold his last company Fanfix, a creator monetization platform, for an estimated $65 million when he was 22 years old. It’s an impressive success story, but these tales are never so glamorous behind the scenes. The struggles he faced while building Fanfix inspired this new venture.

“I was in the office seven days a week, totally neglecting every other area of my life, neglecting my health, sleeping terribly, eating terribly, not working out, and I started to get health problems,” Gestetner told TechCrunch. “I got this inner ear condition, which basically incapacitated me from working for a period of time. As someone who basically had no hobbies and likes to work seven days a week, that was very difficult.”

Gestetner got interested in the longevity movement, which is growing in popularity among some startup or productivity-maxxing types. While he is no Bryan Johnson , it does sound like Gestetner is sipping the Kool-Aid a bit. He tells me that he thinks we’re five years away from “longevity escape velocity,” which means that “for every additional year you’re alive, AI science is able to add an additional year to your life.”

It’s a tough sell, but that’s not what Orion is about anyway. The product is trying to convince you of something that you probably already know: You generally feel better after a good night’s sleep. Even Johnson, who has gone to such extremes as infusing himself with his son’s plasma, says that “Sleep is the world’s most powerful drug.”

“I think most people just want to feel good, and you know, be able to go play soccer with their grandkids up into their older years,” Gestetner said. “I think sleep is the cornerstone of longevity.”

Despite arriving in two intimidatingly large boxes, Orion was easy to set up. It looks like any sort of plush mattress pad, except it has tubes that connect to a tower, which resembles a chic bedside table from West Elm.

Once that’s done, you download the Orion phone app and work through its setup flow, which involves pouring water into the control tower, which is how the cooling system works. I haven’t had to re-up the water supply yet after months of use, which is impressive. If you share a bed with someone, you can even split the Orion into two “zones” that follow their own unique cooling schedules.

From there, you can simply forget that the Orion is there, except for when you get into your perfectly cool bed each night. It requires very infrequent maintenance.

And if you want, you can use the app to check data about your sleep, like how long you spend in light sleep, deep sleep, or REM, and how often you wake up or toss and turn in the middle of the night.

Speaking of data, it’s worth noting that such intimate health information (i.e., exactly when and how you sleep, in detail) is usually transmitted over the cloud for processing, and so may be compromised if a third party that’s involved in the connection gets hacked. Gestetner says Orion invests heavily in security, but this is still an inherent risk in using a connected health product.

While I can confidently say that the Orion has helped me sleep better, there’s no way I’d ever spend $2,195 on something like this. But I would probably feel differently if I were a Silicon Valley engineer making $500,000 a year.

However, in terms of limiting my phone usage before bed, the $59 Brick has done as much to make me sleep better as the Orion, though the products obviously do very different things.

Gestetner may be a millionaire after his last exit, but he still understands Orion’s price puts it out of reach of most people (it’s less expensive than competitor Eight Sleep’s $3,000 model , at least). He says he is working on a more affordable model.

“Eventually we want to get to a $500 price point product,” he said. “To use the Tesla analogy, this product is our Roadster, and we want to eventually get to our Model 3.”
